title: Polynomial Gaussian ridges have one dimension-independent L2 norm
source_anchor: Samplinglib original mathematical supplementv1, 2026-10-20; One actual-law Gaussian polynomial ridge theorem and four mathematical proof steps
target_statement: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure, and p any real polynomial. Put phi(z)=p(z), gamma1=N(0,1), gammaE=stdGaussian(E), and U={w in E: norm(w)=1}. Then phi genuinely belongs to L2(gamma1). Define b=norm(phi)_{L2(gamma1)}+1. One has b>0, and every actual ridge x↦phi(<w,x>) for w in U genuinely belongs to L2(gammaE), with norm exactly norm(phi)_{L2(gamma1)} and hence at most b. The one base norm and the same b serve every direction and dimension. Neither positive dimension, a nonzero polynomial nor evenness is required; the feature conclusions are vacuous when U is empty. No feature moment, covariance or uniform bound is assumed.
